claims.text: In November 2018 $15 million of Qatari money, the first of six monthly instalments totalling $90 million, was brought into Gaza through Israel, mainly for salaries of Hamas-government officials; Netanyahu said it was 'the right step' to restore quiet and prevent a humanitarian crisis, approved by his security cabinet; Bennett compared it to 'protection money'; Livni called it 'submission to Hamas'.

Before May 2021 some $30m in Qatari cash was delivered in suitcases each month through an Israeli-controlled crossing; Israel blocked the payments after the May 2021 war, insisting on safeguards; in August 2021 a UN mechanism to pay families directly was agreed, with Israel overseeing the recipient list.

The New York Times (10 Dec 2023), from interviews with more than two dozen officials, reported Netanyahu 'not only tolerated' the Qatari payments but 'had encouraged them', that Israeli intelligence officers escorted a Qatari official carrying cash into Gaza, and that he had spoken of keeping Hamas strong since at least 2012; Politico reported a 2019 Likud remark: 'Anyone who wants to prevent the establishment of a Palestinian state needs to support strengthening Hamas'; Netanyahu said the payments were 'to avoid a civilian humanitarian collapse' and called the idea he wanted to build up Hamas 'a big lie'.

gz8_aid.topic: Aid, UNRWA and the reconstruction mechanism

claims.text: At the Cairo conference of 12 October 2014 participants pledged about $5.4 billion, half for Gaza reconstruction.

The Gaza Reconstruction Mechanism placed monitors and cameras at distribution points, vetted suppliers and buyers, and kept a database available to Israeli intelligence, giving Israel's security concerns priority and the final say on big projects; Israel had barred construction materials as dual-use that Hamas could use for tunnels; critics said it relieved Israel of responsibility; Oxfam warned rebuilding could take more than 50 years at current import rates.

In January 2024 Israel alleged 12 UNRWA employees took part in the 7 October attacks; the US paused funding on 26 January 2024 and other donors paused, some later resuming; US law (P.L. 118-47) barred UNRWA funding until March 2025; the Colonna review (20 April 2024) found UNRWA had 'many mechanisms in place' for neutrality with gaps; UNRWA's 2023 funding was $1.47 billion.

OIOS investigated 19 staff: in one case no evidence, in nine insufficient evidence, and in nine the evidence 'if authenticated and corroborated' could indicate they 'may have been involved'; their contracts were terminated.
On 28 October 2024 the Knesset voted 92–10 for two bills barring UNRWA from operating in Israel and Israeli officials from contact with it.

claims.text: The US government spent $21.7 billion on military aid to Israel from October 2023 to September 2025, excluding committed arms sales, plus $9.65–12.07 billion on US operations in Yemen and the region.

The World Bank, UN and EU assessment (damage October 2023–October 2025) put recovery and reconstruction needs at $71.4 billion over a decade: physical damage $35.2bn, economic and social losses $22.7bn; over 371,888 housing units destroyed or damaged; the economy contracted 84%; housing needs $16.2bn.
